lines: {target}? Shorelines change under your feet.
That warning belongs at the start of every trip to Beach. Watch the <wavy>tide</wavy>, the turtles, and the drowned at dusk.
Sand looks peaceful until it shifts.
I'll remember Beach as the place where land starts losing to water.
You made it back from the beach. How close did that come to changing?
Did darkness change the route around the beach more than you expected?
I would want both hands free on slick stone and shifting sand. Did you manage that?
A hard journey feels longer in poor weather. How much longer did the beach feel?
Tell me the truth about your supplies. How much water remained when you turned back?
I have crossed ugly water and still would not hurry toward the beach.
The first hot bowl after the beach must have settled more than hunger.
Did you carry one tool that turned out to matter more than all the rest?
Was rest possible once the sounds around the beach started?
Who shared the watch with you when the beach went quiet?
What was the first thing you heard after everyone stopped talking?
Which danger at the beach deserves a clearer warning for the next traveler?
Home must have looked different after the beach. What did you notice first?
Would better planning have changed the danger, or only your chances?
I was worried about the ending. I am glad you are here to tell it.
Who should hear this story before they make the same journey?
{target}? Calm water can still go bottomless.
Tell the next traveler about Deep Lukewarm Ocean before they leave. Don't mistake warm waves for safe waves.
The color is kind, but the depth is not.
I will remember Deep Lukewarm Ocean as warm water with a long fall under it.
Did caution arrive before the danger at the deep lukewarm ocean, or just after it?
What told you that you were still headed the right way at the deep lukewarm ocean?
Which part of the deep lukewarm ocean made you test every step before trusting it?
Did the weather near the deep lukewarm ocean give you any warning before it changed?
Did anyone underestimate how much water the journey would take?
Water has frightened me before. I can hear that the deep lukewarm ocean frightened you worse.
Which meal tasted best once you left the deep lukewarm ocean behind?
What would you remove from the pack before another trip to the deep lukewarm ocean?
What made a place feel safe enough to stop for the night?
Bad nights last longer alone. Who was awake with you?
What warning did the sounds around you give before you saw the danger?
Did you see any warning signs that only made sense afterward?
Did the weather follow you home from the deep lukewarm ocean?
The next traveler needs the honest version. Where should the story begin?
That memory still has weight. Take your time with it.
After all that, is there anything near the deep lukewarm ocean you still want to see?
{target}? Deep water does not care who can swim.
No one should approach Deep Ocean without hearing this. Take a boat and count your air honestly.
The horizon looks simple until you are far from land.
I'll remember Deep Ocean as open water with no nearby door.
Some danger announces itself. What stayed hidden at the deep ocean?
Where would you leave a marker if you had to approach the deep ocean again?
Did your boots hold when slick stone and shifting sand became dangerous?
What did you cover first when the weather turned near the deep ocean?
Did the fresh water you carried last as long as you needed it to?
At least a river tells you which way it is moving. Did the deep ocean tell you anything?
Did worry take your appetite before the supplies ran low?
Was your pack too heavy when the ground became difficult?
Did anyone sleep well while drowned shapes and hidden reefs remained close?
Did anyone keep their nerve when the rest of you were tired?
Does the smell of the deep ocean linger more than the rest of the memory?
Did the danger find you before you found a safe route?
Did anyone speak much on the way back, or were you all spent?
If the village wrote one warning about the deep ocean, what should it say?
Did you feel safe only after the village door closed behind you?
What unfinished question could ever pull you back toward the deep ocean?
{target}? Warm water can still carry teeth.
If someone goes to Lukewarm Ocean, tell them this. Sail smart and do not swim too far from wood.
The waves look friendly until night.
I will remember Lukewarm Ocean as gentle water with danger below the color.
When the danger first showed itself near the lukewarm ocean, did you have room to back away?
If I followed your route to the lukewarm ocean, where would I be most likely to lose it?
Good footing is easy to miss until it disappears. Where did yours disappear?
I trust a route less when the sky changes. What was it like over the lukewarm ocean?
Did the lack of water become its own danger near the lukewarm ocean?
I know how to read a current. I am not sure I could read the lukewarm ocean.
Plain bread can feel like a feast after a place like the lukewarm ocean.
Show me the gear that took the worst of the lukewarm ocean. I want to see the marks.
Did a dry landing above the tide hold until daylight?
Did the group argue before the danger or only after it passed?
Which sound from the lukewarm ocean still follows you into quiet rooms?
Could you avoid a fight, or had the danger already closed the way?
Did the safest course back to shore feel harder once everyone was tired?
Did the journey change how you prepare for ordinary roads?
I know the look of someone remembering bad water. A trip to the lukewarm ocean can leave something similar.
If you went back, what would you pack before anything else?
{target}? Open water moves distance under your feet.
Anyone bound for Ocean should hear this. Keep land in mind and a boat under you.
Waves make every direction look the same.
I'll remember Ocean as water wide enough to make a bell useless.
Once drowned shapes and hidden reefs became a problem, could you still turn around?
Which landmark helped you remember the safest course back to shore?
Where around the ocean did one careful step matter most?
Weather has ruined kinder roads than that. How did your supplies hold up?
A fisherman thinks about water even on dry ground. What water could you count on there?
My worst crossing sounds manageable beside what happened at the ocean.
What did you eat when the road near the ocean ran longer than planned?
How well did a spare oar and dry rope survive the trip to the ocean?
When you finally stopped near the ocean, what did you put between yourself and danger?
Would you trust the same people beside you at the ocean again?
What sound meant safety was finally close?
What kept the first bad encounter from becoming the last one?
What did you promise yourself while the safest course back to shore stretched ahead?
What warning would you give before anyone else heads toward the ocean?
You do not have to make the ocean sound braver than it felt.
Does curiosity still point toward the ocean, or has good sense won?
{target}? A river can carry news or bodies.
Before another traveler leaves for River, warn them. Cross where you can see the bottom.
Current makes even shallow water bossy.
I'll remember River as moving water that does not wait for anyone.
Was the worst part of the river obvious, or did it wait until you were committed?
How much of the journey to the river depended on landmarks instead of a map?
How badly did mud, roots, and flooded ground slow you down?
Which came first near the river, the bad weather or the bad decision?
Did you carry enough clean water to cook near the river?
A boat has edges you can understand, while a trip to the river sounds less honest.
Was any food still dry when you finally stopped?
What broke first near the river, and how did you manage without it?
A dry bed changes the memory of a hard road. Did you find one?
If you returned to the river, whom would you ask to come along?
I judge weather by sound on the water. What sound guided you near the river?
Did putting distance behind you make the danger any easier to judge?
Did you save enough strength for the road home?
Someone will hear this and go anyway. What must they remember?
You look farther away when you speak about the river. Does it still feel close?
Could better weather ever persuade you to take that road again?
{target}? Wet stone is a poor friend to ankles.
Pass this along to whoever visits Stony Shore. Step carefully where waves touch rock.
Shore rocks make boats complain.
I'll remember Stony Shore as hard coastline where water sharpens stone.
What made you lower your voice when you reached the stony shore?
Did you mark the turns near the stony shore, or trust yourself to remember them?
I know what wet docks do to balance. What did slick stone and shifting sand do to yours?
What did wind and rough water do to your plans?
What would you have traded for a clean drink near the stony shore?
A leaking boat can be patched. I would not know where to start with the stony shore.
I hope somebody saved supper for the return from the stony shore.
How much of your gear came back needing repair?
Could anyone sleep near the stony shore, or did you keep watch until morning?
Did you have someone watching the way back while you watched ahead?
Tell me what the place sounded like at night. That usually reveals the truth.
At the stony shore, which threat made everyone change plans fastest?
Which familiar landmark finally let you breathe normally again?
What did the stony shore teach you that a map never could?
Did returning home settle the fear, or merely give it somewhere quiet to sit?
Would you return to the stony shore if someone you trusted asked?
{target}? Bright water can tempt careless swimmers.
The next person heading toward Warm Ocean needs your warning. Take a boat and respect the reef.
Coral color does not promise air.
I'll remember Warm Ocean as warm waves with danger under the shine.
Before things went wrong at the warm ocean, what warning did everyone miss?
The path back matters more than the path in. What did you use to find it?
What sort of footing gave you the most trouble near the warm ocean?
Could you see the way home once wind and rough water began?
What did you rely on for drinking water near the warm ocean?
The dock will feel wonderfully ordinary after hearing that story.
What food would you carry twice as much of if you returned?
I would check every knot after that journey. What needs mending now?
Which place did you choose for camp, and what made you trust it?
Tell me you had steady company on that road.
Did the sounds around you make the danger seem closer than it was?
How much luck was left by the time you got clear?
How long did it take before the village felt close again?
What do people misunderstand most when they talk about the warm ocean?
Some journeys stay in the hands after the road ends. Is this one of them?
Would you guide another traveler there, or only warn them away?
